html:
The Abenaki are an Algonquian people of northern New England and southern Quebec: today's Maine, New Hampshire and Vermont, and the St. Francis River valley. Their name means people of the dawn land, and they were part of the wider Wabanaki world with the Penobscot and others.

They grew maize in the river valleys of the south and hunted and fished in the north, moving with the seasons. Epidemics brought by European fishermen and traders struck them hard in the early 1600s.

Through the colonial wars of the late 1600s and 1700s most Abenaki sided with New France against the English colonists of New England. After King Philip's War and later wars, many moved north to mission villages in Quebec, at Odanak and Wôlinak, which are still Abenaki communities. In 1724 New England militia destroyed the town of Norridgewock in Maine and killed its Jesuit priest. Bands such as the Pequawket held on in the mountains. See also Abnaki.
